name: _buffered_init
reason: The tail of BC2.init (BufC.lean:858-863) has the size <= 0 refusal, the allocation failure (memLimit for PyMem_Malloc failing), the uninitialized PyMem_Malloc buffer and the cleared raw tell, and the no-uninit refutation depends on that uninitialized buffer; but the model only builds a fresh object, so the re-initialization branches of the body (:846-847 freeing the old buffer, :853-860 freeing the old lock, allocating a new one and setting owner = 0) are absent, and they are reachable: measured on 3.15.2 and main, a raw whose readinto calls buf.__init__(...) during read(1) aborts with 'Fatal Python error: PyMutex_Unlock: unlocking mutex that is not locked' (and its readinto writes into the freed buffer).

name: _PyIO_trap_eintr
reason: trapEintr (BufC.lean:231-238) now tests errno == EINTR, but PyErr_ExceptionMatches(PyExc_OSError) (:881) is isOSErrorCls, a list of eight class names, although its docstring says the class plays no part; RawReadChecks part 3 ('every other exception propagates') is therefore proven but false: measured on 3.15.2, FileExistsError, ConnectionResetError and io.UnsupportedOperation with errno EINTR raised by readinto are retried and read(1) succeeds, where the theorem says they propagate.

name: _bufferedreader_fill_buffer
reason: fillBuffer (BufC.lean:281-287) mirrors :1675-1686 (start at read_end when valid, len = size - start, n <= 0 returned, else read_end and raw_pos = start + n); in the no-uninit counterexample its trust of the raw's count is the defect: it returns 16 for a readinto that stored nothing, and peek returns that many buffer bytes, so a fill that returned the bytes actually stored would not refute.
